beam-therapeutics-v-whynot.deck: Potential expert disciplines and candidates for a newly filed trade secret matter concerning cell and gene therapy CMC, bioprocessing, and confidential process-development information.
beam-therapeutics-v-whynot.assessmentTitle: The public record identifies a technically complex dispute, while product-specific proof remains to be developed.
beam-therapeutics-v-whynot.assessmentBody: Given the DTSA cause of action, emergency-relief posture, Whynot's public CMC role, and Beam's disclosed modalities, the likely technical proof will concern whether identified nonpublic process-development or CMC information is secret, valuable, attributable to Beam, technically distinct from public/domain knowledge, and capable of conferring a development or manufacturing head start. The complaint is needed to confirm or narrow this map. No allegation about what Whynot allegedly took, used, disclosed, retained, or intended to do is treated as verified. Precise trade-secret definitions, chronology, employment obligations, devices/accounts, destination, and proposed injunction language require the actual filings.

issues.title: What specific CMC or process-development information does Beam identify as...
issues.question: What specific CMC or process-development information does Beam identify as the alleged trade secret, and at what level of granularity?
issues.proof: Complaint and sealed/unsealed trade-secret schedule; Batch records, development reports, protocols, specifications, and change histories; Publications, patents, regulatory guidance, conference posters, and common industry practice

issues.title: Which asserted information was genuinely nonpublic and economically...
issues.question: Which asserted information was genuinely nonpublic and economically valuable rather than disclosed by Beam or independently available to a skilled CMC professional?
issues.proof: Beam's SEC filings, patents, posters, and publications; Industry standards and FDA guidance; Timestamped internal development records and confidentiality controls

issues.title: If files or communications are identified, what technical content do they...
issues.question: If files or communications are identified, what technical content do they contain, and can that content be tied to a Beam process, program, or development stage?
issues.proof: Forensic images, access logs, downloads, email or cloud-transfer records; Metadata, version histories, authorship records, and document-to-process mapping; Comparison with validated process descriptions and contemporaneous program records

issues.title: Could a recipient reproduce, optimize, troubleshoot, or accelerate a...
issues.question: Could a recipient reproduce, optimize, troubleshoot, or accelerate a base-editing product or manufacturing workflow using the alleged information?
issues.proof: Critical-process-parameter and critical-quality-attribute relationships; Scale-up, robustness, comparability, deviation, and failure-analysis records; Counterfactual time/cost analysis and independently available alternatives

issues.title: Can any allegedly overlapping later work be explained by independent...
issues.question: Can any allegedly overlapping later work be explained by independent development, ordinary CMC knowledge, or common regulatory requirements?
issues.proof: Chronologies, notebooks, source files, raw data, and design-of-experiments records; Public literature and standard operating approaches available before the alleged conduct; Element-by-element process and analytical-method comparison

issues.title: What scientifically meaningful conduct or information could an injunction...
issues.question: What scientifically meaningful conduct or information could an injunction identify without sweeping in general skill, experience, public science, or unrelated modalities?
issues.proof: Proposed order and defined trade-secret list; Modality-specific workflow maps for ex vivo HSPC, LNP, mRNA, and analytical work; Expert explanation of separable steps, parameters, and public baselines

docket.summary: Beam filed a complaint against Andrew Whynot with sixteen exhibits. Beam filed an ex parte motion for a temporary restraining order and preliminary injunction. Beam filed a supporting memorandum with declarations from Tavish M. Brown, Susan O'Connor, Chris Oesterling, and Brad Dutot. The court declined to resolve the motion ex parte, required proof of service of the complaint, motion papers, and order, and set the response deadline at ten days after proof of service is filed.

recipient.name: Tavish M. Brown
recipient.role: Outside counsel, Hirsch Roberts Weinstein LLP

experts.name: Kelvin H. Lee
experts.role: Gore Professor of Chemical & Biomolecular Engineering, University of Delaware; Institute Director, National Institute for Innovation in Manufacturing Biopharmaceuticals (NIIMBL)
experts.fit: Top-level biomanufacturing and analytical fit for process development, manufacturing control, proteomics, systems biology, and the public-knowledge baseline for CMC know-how.
experts.work: His university profile identifies NIIMBL leadership and work in proteomics, biological mass spectrometry, protein secretion and synthesis; these bear on process understanding and analytical characterization, though not specifically on Beam's alleged secrets.
experts.litigation: No candidate-specific expert report, deposition, or trial-testimony source was located in the bounded search.
experts.weakness: Broad biomanufacturing expertise may be less specific to autologous HSPC electroporation and base-editor chemistry. NIIMBL's extensive industry relationships require conflicts and funding diligence.

experts.name: Bruce L. Levine
experts.role: Barbara and Edward Netter Professor in Cancer Gene Therapy, University of Pennsylvania; founding director of Penn's Clinical Cell and Vaccine Production Facility
experts.fit: Direct fit for clinical cell and gene therapy, cGMP manufacturing, testing, technology transfer, and engineered-cell product operations.
experts.work: Penn states that his interests include cell, gene, and biologic therapy clinical-trial development, manufacturing, and testing and expressly lists Good Manufacturing Practices expertise.
experts.litigation: No candidate-specific expert report, deposition, or trial-testimony source was located. A 2023 ISCT paper instead discloses scientific-advisory and consulting compensation that must be evaluated separately.
experts.weakness: His public disclosure lists advisory roles with multiple cell/gene-therapy companies and consulting for GSK; commercial and institutional conflicts could be substantial. His primary scientific focus is engineered immune-cell therapy rather than Beam's full platform.

experts.name: Krishnendu Roy
experts.role: Bruce and Bridgitt Evans Dean of Engineering and University Distinguished Professor of Biomedical Engineering, Pathology/Microbiology/Immunology, and Chemical & Biomolecular Engineering, Vanderbilt University
experts.fit: Strong fit for therapeutic-cell characterization, scalable cell manufacturing, potency/quality concepts, and engineering of nucleic-acid delivery.
experts.work: Vanderbilt records his prior leadership of the NSF Cell Manufacturing Technologies center and the Marcus Center for Therapeutic Cell Characterization and Manufacturing, plus work in stem-cell engineering and nucleic-acid delivery.
experts.litigation: No candidate-specific expert report, deposition, or trial-testimony source was located; name collisions were excluded.
experts.weakness: A dean role may limit current hands-on process work. His expertise is cell manufacturing broadly, not specifically Beam base editing, and his consortium/industry relationships require diligence.

experts.name: Michael Betenbaugh
experts.role: Professor of Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering, Johns Hopkins University; lead principal investigator of the Advanced Mammalian Biomanufacturing Innovation Center
experts.fit: Strong process-science fit for mammalian cell biomanufacturing, cell-line optimization, systems biology, and identifying which process information is routine versus proprietary.
experts.work: Johns Hopkins describes his pioneering work in eukaryotic metabolic engineering, mammalian production hosts, glycobiology, and secretory-pathway process bottlenecks.
experts.litigation: No candidate-specific expert report, deposition, or trial-testimony source was located in the bounded search.
experts.weakness: His public work centers substantially on production cell lines and recombinant biologics, which is adjacent to but not the same as autologous HSPC base editing or LNP delivery.

experts.name: Abraham M. Lenhoff
experts.role: Allan P. Colburn Professor of Chemical Engineering, University of Delaware
experts.fit: Strong downstream-processing and protein-biophysics fit for impurity clearance, chromatography, phase behavior, transport, and analytical comparison of process streams.
experts.work: Delaware lists applied protein biophysics, solution thermodynamics, adsorption, chromatography, and transport; a 2025 manuscript addresses scalability of impurity precipitation in downstream biomanufacturing.
experts.litigation: No candidate-specific expert report, deposition, or trial-testimony source was located in the bounded search.
experts.weakness: His strongest fit is protein purification and downstream unit operations, not whole-cell manufacturing, genome editing, or digital misappropriation. Utility depends on the complaint's actual secret definitions.

experts.name: Matthew Porteus
experts.role: Sutardja Chuk Professor of Definitive and Curative Medicine and Professor of Pediatrics, Stanford University School of Medicine
experts.fit: Direct scientific fit for genome editing in hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells, nuclease-mediated editing, clinical translation, and edited-cell characterization.
experts.work: Stanford describes his work developing homologous-recombination genome editing as curative therapy for genetic blood diseases and identifies him as a pioneer of genome editing.
experts.litigation: No candidate-specific expert report, deposition, or trial-testimony source was located in the bounded search.
experts.weakness: Deep genome-editing expertise does not by itself establish commercial CMC or trade-secret valuation expertise. Patent, startup, sponsor, competitor, and Beam-related academic conflicts need careful review.

experts.name: Paula Cannon
experts.role: Distinguished Professor of Immunology and Immune Therapeutics, Stem Cell Biology and Regenerative Medicine, and Biomedical Engineering, University of Southern California
experts.fit: Strong fit for CRISPR/ZFN engineering of hematopoietic stem and immune cells, gene-therapy translation, and distinguishing platform science from process-specific know-how.
experts.work: USC describes her use of CRISPR/Cas9 to engineer immune cells and lists work on clinical applications and qualification of genome editing in hematopoietic stem/progenitor cells.
experts.litigation: No candidate-specific expert report, deposition, or trial-testimony source was located in the bounded search.
experts.weakness: Her public record is strongest in viral and nuclease-based cell engineering, not Beam's proprietary base editors or end-to-end commercial CMC. Society leadership and collaborations broaden conflict diligence.

experts.name: Fyodor Urnov
experts.role: Professor of Genetics, Genomics, Evolution, and Development, University of California, Berkeley; Director for Technology and Translation at the Innovative Genomics Institute
experts.fit: High fit for genome- and epigenome-editing mechanisms, tool development, technical translation, and separating generally known editing concepts from implementation-specific know-how.
experts.work: Berkeley lists his research interest as CRISPR-based genome and epigenome editing and his technology-translation leadership at IGI.
experts.litigation: No candidate-specific expert report, deposition, or trial-testimony source was located in the bounded search.
experts.weakness: His central expertise is editing technology rather than CMC operations, scale-up, or damages. Prior industry work, IP positions, public advocacy, and relationships across genome-editing companies require diligence.

experts.name: David V. Schaffer
experts.role: Hubbard Howe Jr. Distinguished Professor of Biochemical Engineering, University of California, Berkeley; professor of bioengineering and molecular and cell biology; executive director of QB3 and director of Bakar Labs and the Berkeley Stem Cell Center
experts.fit: Strong complementary fit for therapeutic gene delivery, viral-vector engineering, stem-cell therapeutics, and delivery-platform technical comparison.
experts.work: Berkeley describes his work engineering AAV and other viral vehicles through directed evolution and developing genetic cargoes and targeted nucleases for therapy.
experts.litigation: No candidate-specific expert report, deposition, or trial-testimony source was located in the bounded search.
experts.weakness: His best-known delivery work is AAV-focused, while Beam publicly emphasizes electroporation and LNP modalities. Translational ventures, patents, licenses, and company relationships may create conflicts.

experts.name: Millicent Sullivan
experts.role: Alvin B. and Julie O. Stiles Professor of Chemical & Biomolecular Engineering and Professor of Biomedical Engineering, University of Delaware
experts.fit: Complementary fit for intracellular delivery of DNA/RNA and macromolecular therapeutics, biomaterials, nanoparticle design, and the boundary between public delivery principles and proprietary formulations/processes.
experts.work: Delaware lists gene and siRNA delivery, polymer and peptide biomaterials, and cell/organelle-specific macromolecular delivery.
experts.litigation: No candidate-specific expert report, deposition, or trial-testimony source was located in the bounded search.
experts.weakness: Her public work is more research-oriented than commercial cell/gene-therapy CMC and is not specifically tied to base editing, HSPC electroporation, or Beam's LNP processes.

recipient.role: Of Counsel, Bunsow De Mory LLP

experts.name: James S. Plank, PhD
experts.role: Professor, Min H. Kao Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science, University of Tennessee, Knoxville
experts.fit: Direct specialist in erasure coding, fault-tolerant and distributed storage, Galois-field arithmetic, and practical coding libraries.
experts.work: Creator or contributor to widely used erasure-coding software and publications including Jerasure, GF-Complete, Liberation Codes, and storage-focused erasure-code tutorials.
experts.litigation: Served as a storage-technology expert in EMC Corp. v. Pure Storage and as defendants' expert in ChampionX v. Resonance Systems.
experts.weakness: Extensive prior expert work creates discoverable positions. A 2024 order discusses a prior StreamScale arbitration concerning alleged information disclosure; the matter settled without assigned blame but would require careful diligence.

experts.name: Gregory R. Ganger, PhD
experts.role: Jatras Professor of Electrical and Computer Engineering, Carnegie Mellon University
experts.fit: Cloud computing, distributed storage, operating systems, storage access control, and performance at large scale.
experts.work: Leads research spanning cloud computing, resource scheduling, big-data systems, and distributed storage through CMU's Parallel Data Lab ecosystem.
experts.litigation: Public records identify expert reports or testimony in Sun Microsystems v. Network Appliance and 01 Communique matters.
experts.weakness: Established expert history means prior claim-construction, infringement, and validity opinions should be mapped for consistency. Less narrowly focused on erasure-code mathematics than Plank.

experts.role: Professor of Computer Science and Director, File Systems and Storage Lab, Stony Brook University
experts.fit: File systems, distributed and cloud storage, operating systems, performance, benchmarking, and storage reliability.
experts.work: Directs Stony Brook's File Systems and Storage Lab and serves as Editor-in-Chief of ACM Transactions on Storage.
experts.litigation: Substantial district-court and PTAB experience; a public deposition states that he has represented plaintiffs and defendants, and public PTAB records include repeated declarations.
experts.weakness: Frequent expert work and a substantial PTAB record create a large cross-examination corpus. Public aggregations suggest a defense/petitioner tilt, which must be verified from underlying matters.

experts.name: Tor M. Aamodt, PhD
experts.role: Professor of Electrical and Computer Engineering, University of British Columbia
experts.fit: GPU and accelerator architecture, memory systems, general-purpose parallel processing, and NVIDIA architecture history.
experts.work: Co-author of a GPGPU architecture book; developed influential GPU simulation work; formerly worked at NVIDIA on GeForce 8 memory-system architecture, the first CUDA-capable generation.
experts.litigation: His official biography states patent-litigation work involving GPUs and computer systems; a public order discusses his expert report in XMTT v. Intel.
experts.weakness: Stronger on GPU architecture than enterprise storage services or erasure-code implementation. Industry consulting and research funding, including NVIDIA and Huawei connections, require conflicts and bias diligence.

experts.name: Randal Burns, PhD
experts.role: Bill and Lisa Stromberg Department Head and Professor of Computer Science, Johns Hopkins University
experts.fit: Scale-out cloud storage, redundancy coding, storage auditing, large data systems, and storage-area-network architecture.
experts.work: Research spans storage-area networks, scientific services on scale-out cloud storage, redundancy coding, and data-intensive systems; previously worked at IBM Almaden.
experts.litigation: No clear public testifying role located in the initial bounded search; this is not a representation that none exists.
experts.weakness: Department-head duties may constrain time. Research emphasizes scientific data systems and storage services more than DPU microarchitecture. Availability and conflicts were not checked.

experts.name: Bianca Schroeder, PhD
experts.role: Full Professor and Canada Research Chair in Data Centre Technologies, University of Toronto
experts.fit: Large-scale systems, storage systems, data centers, failure behavior, and empirical systems reliability.
experts.work: Research focuses on design and analysis of storage and data-center systems, including large-scale reliability and performance behavior.
experts.litigation: No clear public patent-litigation testimony located in the initial bounded search; this is not a representation that none exists.
experts.weakness: Best suited to reliability, performance, and data-center evidence; less directly matched to claim construction for vector processors or finite-field coding algorithms.

experts.name: Hakim Weatherspoon, PhD
experts.role: Professor of Computer Science, Cornell University
experts.fit: Secure and fault-tolerant distributed storage, internet-scale systems, reliability, security, and performance.
experts.work: PhD work addressed distributed wide-area archival storage; current research covers decentralized and fault-tolerant systems at internet scale.
experts.litigation: No clear public testifying role located in the initial bounded search; this is not a representation that none exists.
experts.weakness: Broad distributed-systems profile rather than a narrow DPU or erasure-code implementation specialist. Academic and industry relationships require standard diligence.

experts.name: Haryadi S. Gunawi, PhD
experts.role: Professor of Computer Science, University of Chicago
experts.fit: Cloud and storage reliability, latency-tail behavior, performance stability, scalability bugs, and new storage technologies.
experts.work: Leads the UCARE group on availability, reliability, and efficiency in storage and cloud systems; publications address limpware, tail latency, and dependable storage.
experts.litigation: No clear public testifying role located in the initial bounded search; this is not a representation that none exists.
experts.weakness: Best fit for performance and reliability questions, not erasure-code mathematics or NVIDIA DPU design. Prior Google and NetApp research awards warrant routine relationship diligence.

experts.name: Darrell D. E. Long, PhD
experts.role: Distinguished Research Professor of Engineering, University of California, Santa Cruz
experts.fit: Storage-system architecture, operating systems, distributed computing, archival storage, reliability, and security.
experts.work: Longstanding leader in UCSC storage research with publications and patents concerning storage systems and high-rate data access.
experts.litigation: Extensive patent-expert history. A public 2013 deposition states roughly a dozen prior expert engagements; later records show additional PTAB and district-court work.
experts.weakness: Large, predominantly defense/petitioner-side public record and earlier opinions in storage matters require issue-by-issue consistency review. Current distinguished-research role should be confirmed.

experts.name: Ethan L. Miller, PhD
experts.role: Professor Emeritus and Director Emeritus, Center for Research in Systems and Storage, University of California, Santa Cruz
experts.fit: Storage reliability, archival storage, erasure coding, file systems, and storage-system performance.
experts.work: Co-authored work on finite-field arithmetic for erasure coding and alpha-entanglement codes; longtime leader of UCSC storage research.
experts.litigation: No clear public testifying role attributable to this computer scientist was located in the initial bounded search; same-name results create false-positive risk.
experts.weakness: Emeritus status and current activity must be confirmed. Same-name contamination is material in litigation-history searching; identity matching requires care.

issues.title: Which Caterpillar product or product family is actually accused, and what...
issues.question: Which Caterpillar product or product family is actually accused, and what physical and control architecture does it use?
issues.proof: Exhibit 2 and any claim chart; Product manuals, bills of material, wiring diagrams, and supplier documentation; Physical inspection, teardown, nameplate evidence, and bench testing

issues.title: Does the accused machine operate as an induction generator, rather than as...
issues.question: Does the accused machine operate as an induction generator, rather than as a permanent-magnet, wound-field synchronous, switched-reluctance, or other generator?
issues.proof: Rotor and stator construction; Slip, excitation, magnetization-current, and speed-frequency behavior; Controller and power-stage documentation

issues.title: If an induction machine is present, is it driven above synchronous or rated...
issues.question: If an induction machine is present, is it driven above synchronous or rated speed in the manner required by the asserted claim, and how should 'overspeed' be construed and measured?
issues.proof: Machine ratings and pole count; Measured shaft speed, electrical frequency, slip, torque, and output waveforms; Engine and generator control maps over the accused operating envelope

issues.title: What circuit couples generator output to the alleged energy reservoir, and...
issues.question: What circuit couples generator output to the alleged energy reservoir, and does it perform the claimed AC-to-DC conversion and decoupling function?
issues.proof: Power-electronics schematics and component identification; Gate signals, DC-link measurements, current-flow tests, and control-state logs; Battery, capacitor-bank, or other storage specifications

issues.title: Is there a transducer-to-control-module-to-servomechanism throttle-control...
issues.question: Is there a transducer-to-control-module-to-servomechanism throttle-control loop satisfying the claimed signal path and response relationship?
issues.proof: Sensor lists and calibration data; ECU architecture, software logic, CAN messages, and throttle or fuel-actuator commands; Dynamic testing correlating sensed variables with control outputs

issues.title: Does any energy reservoir buffer average generator power against peak load...
issues.question: Does any energy reservoir buffer average generator power against peak load demand in the claimed arrangement, and in which operating modes?
issues.proof: Energy-storage sizing and integration documents; Charge/discharge traces under representative loads; System energy-flow and operating-mode analysis

issues.title: Which claim terms require technical construction, including 'induction...
issues.question: Which claim terms require technical construction, including 'induction motor,' 'overspeed,' 'energy reservoir,' 'control module,' 'transducer,' and 'servomechanism throttle control'?
issues.proof: Intrinsic record and prosecution history; Contemporaneous electrical-machine, generator, power-conversion, and engine-control literature; Standards, textbooks, manuals, and skilled-artisan usage

issues.title: What did pre-October 2001 systems and publications teach about self-excited...
issues.question: What did pre-October 2001 systems and publications teach about self-excited induction generation, rectification to DC storage, overspeed operation, hybrid power systems, and feedback control?
issues.proof: Patents, textbooks, IEEE papers, generator manuals, and commercial system documents predating October 1, 2001; Element-by-element prior-art charts; Motivation-to-combine and reasonable-expectation-of-success analysis

issues.title: What testing can distinguish accused operation from noninfringing modes...
issues.question: What testing can distinguish accused operation from noninfringing modes without damaging the product or relying on undocumented assumptions?
issues.proof: Joint inspection protocol; Instrument calibration and uncertainty budget; Repeatable dynamometer or load-bank tests with synchronized electrical and mechanical measurements

issues.title: What would a person of ordinary skill have understood by 'automated...

issues.title: Does an accused product actually conduct a negotiation with a remote...

issues.title: Does the accused antenna system have an alterable directional vector with...

issues.title: Which accused product configurations, optional features, network roles, and...

issues.title: What pre-priority systems and publications disclosed the claimed...

issues.title: Does the specification teach a skilled person how to implement the full...

bayer-healthcare-pharmaceuticals-v-saba.assessmentBody: The likely technical center is the validity of Bayer's finerenone compound patent, not whether a proposed bioequivalent generic contains finerenone. The public complaint analysis reports anticipation and obviousness theories based on U.S. Patent No. 8,404,709, plus written-description, enablement, and indefiniteness theories. Expert work will likely compare the earlier disclosure with the '180 patent's genus and finerenone-specific claims, reconstruct the medicinal-chemistry choices as of the 2007 priority date, assess stereochemical identity and analytical proof, and evaluate whether any asserted pharmacologic advantages are commensurate with the claimed invention. The complaint analysis is a secondary public source, not a substitute for the filed complaint, SABA's Paragraph IV notice, the complete prosecution histories, expert reports, or discovery. The docket does not identify asserted claims, and no conclusion is drawn on infringement, validity, enforceability, claim scope, or commercial outcome.

S. as defendant. It classifies the action as an ANDA patent case, records the August 21, 2026 complaint, and identifies U.S. Patent No. 8,436,180 in the report to the Commissioner of Patents and Trademarks. The docket names Alexandra M. Joyce and Daniel M. Silver of McCarter & English as counsel for the Bayer plaintiffs. boehringer-ingelheim-v-fdc.assessmentTitle: The public record identifies a technically complex dispute, while product-specific proof remains to be developed.
boehringer-ingelheim-v-fdc.assessmentBody: The public complaint analysis reports that FDC submitted ANDA No. 220862 seeking approval for 10 mg and 25 mg empagliflozin tablets before expiration of four asserted Jardiance method-of-treatment patents. The likely technical center is what FDC's proposed label directs or encourages clinicians to do: assess renal function, treat patients with type 2 diabetes in the claimed estimated-glomerular-filtration-rate range, discontinue or modify treatment at lower renal function, and treat adolescents aged 10 to 17. Expert work will likely require close comparison of the claims, proposed label, renal-function methods, clinical-practice context, and prior art for the claimed patient subgroups and treatment steps. The complaint analysis is a secondary public source, not a substitute for the filed complaint and exhibits, FDC's Paragraph IV notice, the final or proposed FDC label, complete patent prosecution histories, expert reports, or discovery. No conclusion is drawn on infringement, inducement, validity, enforceability, claim scope, regulatory outcome, or commercial outcome.
boehringer-ingelheim-v-fdc.disciplines: The preliminary slate combines complementary specialists matched to the asserted technical questions. Candidate roles, public work, email evidence, litigation-history findings, and diligence concerns appear below.

docket.summary: The public docket identifies Boehringer Ingelheim Pharmaceuticals Inc., Boehringer Ingelheim International GmbH, and Boehringer Ingelheim Pharma GmbH & Co. KG as plaintiffs and FDC Limited and FDC Inc. as defendants. It records an August 21, 2026 complaint, civil cover sheet, report on the filing or determination of an action regarding a patent or trademark, and five exhibits. The docket identifies Liza M. Walsh of Walsh Pizzi O'Reilly Falanga LLP as counsel for all three plaintiffs.
